definition_one_sentence: A customer account with at least one non-cancelled order in the last 12 months; this is the official figure used in the board report.
formula_or_rule: count distinct customer_id in fct_orders where status <> 'cancelled' and order_date > current_date - 12 months and order_date <= current_date
example: On 2026-11-25 a customer whose last non-cancelled order is on 2026-03-10 is active; a customer whose only order in the period was cancelled is not. ShopFast today: 1,080 active customers (1,104 if cancelled orders were wrongly counted).
related_columns: fct_orders.status, fct_orders.order_date (dim_customers.last_order_date is NOT enough: it includes cancelled orders)
notes_conflicts: Sales wanted 6 months and Finance 12 months. CDO arbitration: 12 months = official term (investors compare years). Sales keeps its 6-month view under a separate term: recently active customer.

definition_one_sentence: A customer account with at least one non-cancelled order in the last 6 months; used by Sales for seasonal marketing campaigns, never in the board report.
formula_or_rule: count distinct customer_id in fct_orders where status <> 'cancelled' and order_date > current_date - 6 months and order_date <= current_date
example: On 2026-11-25 a customer whose last non-cancelled order is on 2026-07-01 is recently active; one whose last order is on 2026-03-10 is active but not recently active. ShopFast today: 775 recently active customers.
notes_conflicts: Created to settle the active customer conflict: one term = one definition. Every recently active customer is also an active customer.

definition_one_sentence: What ShopFast actually earns on an order: the amount paid minus refunds, excluding VAT, shipping fees included.
example: Customer pays 120.00 EUR, no refund: (120 - 0) / 1.20 = 100.00 EUR. Customer pays 120.00 EUR and gets 24.00 EUR back: (120 - 24) / 1.20 = 80.00 EUR.
notes_conflicts: Sales called net revenue the amount incl. VAT minus refunds. Decision: VAT is not ShopFast's money, so net revenue is always excl. VAT. Sales commissions use gross revenue (incl. VAT), an existing separate term.

definition_one_sentence: A customer who ordered in the past but has no non-cancelled order in the last 12 months, i.e. a former customer who is no longer active.
formula_or_rule: customer with at least 1 non-cancelled order ever AND NOT active customer (no non-cancelled order in the last 12 months)
example: A customer whose last non-cancelled order is on 2025-06-15 is churned on 2026-11-25. An account created in 2025 that never ordered is NOT churned (never a buyer).
notes_conflicts: Defined as the exact opposite of active customer (12 months) so that active + churned + never-ordered = all accounts. Target variable of the churn prediction model.

definition_one_sentence: A registered customer account on ShopFast, identified by customer_id, whether or not it has ever ordered.
formula_or_rule: one row in stg_customers / dim_customers = one customer (count distinct customer_id)
example: 1,233 customer accounts after removing exact duplicate rows (1,241 raw rows). 52 people have 2 accounts with the same email: they still count as 2 customers until a merge is decided.
notes_conflicts: Customer = account, not person. Counting persons would require merging duplicate accounts (is_duplicate_email flag from CTP 2), which is a Steward decision.

definition_one_sentence: A purchase placed by a customer on any channel, identified by order_id, whatever its status (pending, shipped, delivered, cancelled or returned).
formula_or_rule: one row in fct_orders = one order (count distinct order_id); filter on status when a KPI needs it
example: 5,200 orders in fct_orders after removing 7 duplicated order_ids. Order 10001 placed on the web and delivered counts as 1 order; a cancelled order is still an order but brings no revenue to KPIs that exclude it.
notes_conflicts: Cancelled orders are kept in the table: each KPI must say whether it excludes them (active customer does).
